title: Manual for Fortran Software Package DFO v1. 2
contribution: UNREADABLE AS NAMED: the text file is the DFO v2.0 manual (K. Scheinberg, Aug 20, 2003), not v1.2 (2000, Conn-Scheinberg-Toint); the substitute documents a trust-region interpolation DFO code for expensive smooth problems with easy, difficult and virtual (hidden) constraints (pp. 1-3).
problem_entry: [v2.0 substitute] Software for smooth expensive functions without usable derivatives, n < 50; states when not to use it (derivatives available, n large) (p. 1).
key_idea: [v2.0 substitute] Best point as base, interpolation set chosen near the base while keeping well-poisedness, model minimised over trust region subject to modelled difficult constraints (exact penalty if infeasible), ratio test; minimum-Frobenius-norm models by default (pp. 2-3, 9-10).
assumptions: [v2.0 substitute] Smoothness needed for theory; optional absolute/relative noise levels used only for termination (pp. 1, 8).
positioning: [v2.0 substitute] Cites Conn-Scheinberg-Toint 1996-98 as the algorithm and the Conn-Scheinberg-Vicente 2003 preprint (S072) for well-poisedness; interfaces NPSOL/NPOPT/IPOPT (pp. 2-3, 12-13).
writing: [v2.0 substitute] Plain user manual: every parameter with typical value, meaning and effect; frank remarks such as effort levels 'not fully tested yet' and defaults justified by 'Experiments and some intuition' (pp. 5-10).
limits_future: [v2.0 substitute] Default maximum 50 variables, slow for large n, EFFORT levels untested, penalty METHOD 3/4 not usable with IPOPT; no future work (pp. 1, 7, 9, 10).

method_links.note: [v2.0 substitute] geometry as tunable price: pivot thresholds PIVTHR/ADDTHR, exchange factor XCHTHR, EFFORT levels (lowest = recompute only when necessary); NPMIN = n+1 gives fully linear models
[v2.0 substitute] difficult constraints computed with f are modelled individually by default rather than folded into a penalty
[v2.0 substitute] noise level used only as a stopping rule (no accuracy tied to Delta) - Workflow B step 6 in early form

title: Incremental learning and selective sampling via parametric optimization framework for SVM
contribution: POKER, a parametric-QP framework that moves one scalar in the right-hand side of the SVM KKT system while tracking the optimal partition, giving a fixed-bias method, a bias-adjusting method and their alternation AltPOKER, an exact incremental 1-norm soft-margin SVM with arbitrary chunk sizes and look-ahead-based selective sampling (pp. 2-7).
problem_entry: Active-set SVM training is slow and fixed-bias incremental shortcuts generalise worse; the only exact incremental method is Cauwenberghs-Poggio; entry via parametric QP from optimization (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Homotopy in a scalar (u for the fixed-bias system, then b) with partition (I0, Ic, Is) updates at breakpoints; dObj criterion runs a few adjustable-bias iterations to estimate objective change, likened to strong branching (pp. 3-6).
assumptions: 1-norm soft-margin SVM KKT system; nondegenerate (Qss nonsingular) vs degenerate case; O(n^2) estimate assumes few support vectors (pp. 3-4, 7).
proof_devices: finite termination because each iteration consumes a parameter interval with a distinct optimal partition and partitions are finite (p. 4)
per-iteration cost O(n|Is|)+O(|Is|^3) nondegenerate; exponential worst case argued away by the simplex analogy (pp. 2, 4)
experiments: Abalone batch mode (iterations vs size, polynomial kernels), diabetes incremental (iterations vs chunk size), selective sampling on synthetic 10Kx2, ionosphere, diabetes (Table 1); iteration counts only, qualitative comparison to Cauwenberghs-Poggio (pp. 5-7).
positioning: Positions against active-set methods, fixed-bias incremental updates and Cauwenberghs-Poggio (independently developed, somewhat similar, but more general: fixed-bias and bias-adjusting modes, chunks, objective-change estimate) (pp. 1-2, 7).
writing: Short NIPS paper; lemmas deferred to a technical report (footnote 3, p. 2); theory-vs-practice framing for complexity ('In theory ... But in practice ...', p. 5); contributions restated in the conclusion as three generality claims (p. 7).
limits_future: Exponential worst case, complexity depends on few SVs; future: true on-line algorithm, active learning, massive-data (speech) applications (pp. 2, 7).

method_links.note: keeps a classical optimization device (parametric QP, simplex-type partition pivoting; strong branching) and carries it into SVM training
exploits piecewise-linear dependence of the KKT solution on one scalar while the partition is fixed
comparisons by iteration counts only, no equal-cost head-to-head

title: Error estimates and poisedness in multivariate polynomial interpolation
contribution: Introduces Lambda-poisedness, a geometric basis-independent measure of interpolation-set quality equivalent to bounded Lagrange polynomials, derives Taylor-like error bounds for all derivatives (function error a posteriori) in the linear and quadratic cases, and gives a Gaussian-elimination algorithm that builds or repairs well-poised sets (pp. 1-2, 10, 19, 24, 27-29).
problem_entry: Interpolation models must behave like Taylor models for standard trust-region theory to apply; existing bounds are basis-tied, hard to read, or cover function values only; condition numbers are basis-dependent and misleading (pp. 1-2, 6).
key_idea: Define poisedness by the coefficient norm needed to represent phi(x)-phi(0) through phi(y^i)-phi(0) over the ball; derive all derivative errors from one x-independent linear system obtained by subtracting interpolation conditions; repair geometry by threshold pivoting (pp. 6-10, 27-28).
assumptions: Y in B(Delta) with an interpolation point at the centre (the trust-region situation); linear: Lipschitz gradient, n+1 points; quadratic: Lipschitz Hessian, (n+1)(n+2)/2 points (pp. 3-5, 11-12).
proof_devices: subtract the first interpolation condition from the others so the function-value error cancels: L e_g(x) = O(Delta^2) with x-independent L (eq. (10), p. 8)
Lambda-poised iff ||L^{-1}|| <= Lambda/Delta via scaling to the unit ball (Lemmas 2.2-2.3, pp. 9-10)

Lemma 3.3: a quadratic with ||v||_inf = 1 reaches |value| >= 1/2 on the unit ball, by restricting to the variables of the largest coefficient; gives theta_Q and the attainable pivot threshold xi < 1/2 (pp. 17-18, 28)
positioning: Re-derives and simplifies Powell, Sauer-Xu, Waldron bounds (as good for function values, adds derivatives); corrects the authors' own 1997 CST analysis whose O(Delta) gradient bound gives only first-order convergence; links optimal simplex to positive bases in pattern search (pp. 2, 24-27, 31).
writing: Motivation-first intro that criticises prior bounds as unintuitive; linear case first 'to introduce the basic steps', quadratic next, general degree via cubic; explicit remarks on which assumptions are not WLOG (p. 4) and open choices (p. 11) (pp. 2-4, 11).
limits_future: Unclear which of two gradient bounds is better (p. 11); growth factors only 'expected to be of reasonable size' (p. 29); O(n^6) repair cost (p. 29); no future work in the conclusion (pp. 31-32).

method_links.note: geometry is the only controllable error source and Lambda prices it; Algorithm 6.1 replaces only bad points
origin of the error <= kappa*Delta^k shape (controllable Lambda times uncontrollable gamma) later required only with probability p
aim is to make standard unconstrained trust-region convergence theory apply unchanged to interpolation models

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: new geometric Lambda-poisedness proved equivalent to bounded Lagrange polynomials so prior results transfer (compare s01/S053 partial RIP)

transferable: Bound all derivative errors of an interpolation model at once by subtracting interpolation conditions so the unknown value error cancels, inverting the x-independent matrix, and deriving the value error last (pp. 8-10, 32).
Define a geometry measure via coefficient norms of representing any point by the samples, prove basis-independence, and tie it to ||L^{-1}|| by rescaling to the unit ball (pp. 7, 9-10).

Turn threshold-pivoting Gaussian elimination into a geometry-repair routine that replaces a point by the maximiser of the pivot polynomial, with a universal lower bound making the threshold attainable (pp. 28-29).
coauthors: A. R. Conn, L. N. Vicente

quotes.text: However, it turns out to be equivalent to Λ being the upper bound on the absolute values of the Lagrange polynomials.
In practical situations only the geometry of the interpolation set is controllable.

title: A product-form Cholesky factorization method for handling dense columns in interior point methods for linear programming
contribution: A product-form Cholesky factorization (sparse Cholesky plus product-form rank-one updates, with pivot skipping) for dense columns in IPMs for LP that is nearly as fast as Schur complement/SMW but stable, backed by a proof that Cholesky factors of AD^2A^T stay uniformly bounded as the duality gap goes to zero (pp. 1, 7-14, 22-25, 29-34).
problem_entry: Dense columns destroy sparse Cholesky efficiency; the standard Schur complement/SMW remedy is unstable near optimality (2x2 example; Andersen's fix fails on about half the test problems late in the run) (pp. 1-2, 5-6).
key_idea: Keep the normal-equations approach and sparse Cholesky; add dense columns as symmetric rank-one updates (Bennett's method via Fletcher-Powell and Gill-Murray-Saunders formulas) kept in product form; handle small pivots with an extension of Wright's pivot skipping (pp. 7-10, 22).
assumptions: Fixed A, diagonal D(mu); no near-degeneracy; IPM iterates follow optimal-partition rates; error analysis follows Fletcher-Powell [7] (pp. 10-11, 18).
proof_devices: smallest-bad-column-index contradiction along a subsequence (Theorem 4.4, pp. 12-14)
subsequence partition of functions by relative rate (Lemma 4.1, p. 11)
projection lemma: a bounded r(mu) with r(mu)^T B -> 0 forces linear dependence of rows of B (Lemma 4.3, p. 12)
uniqueness of LDL^T: product-form factor = L^{-1} Lbar, bounded by Lemma 4.2 (Theorem 4.5, p. 14)
operation-count cost model in k and m predicting ~4% (k=10, m=3000) to ~50% (k=50) slowdown vs Schur complement (p. 27)
experiments: 20 problems (5 Netlib + two-stage stochastic LP deterministic equivalents, 4-50 dense columns); CF, PFCF, Schur complement (with Andersen's columns) and augmented system inside Mehrotra's fo1/fo1aug, OSL for time, CPLEX 6.5.1 for stability; accuracy 1e-8; failures and out-of-memory marked (pp. 16, 29-34).
positioning: Direct critique of the Schur complement/SMW method and Andersen's fix by example and experiment; builds on Bennett and Fletcher-Powell rank-one updates (p. 8) and Wright's pivot skipping (p. 22); relates Theorem 4.4 to the Vavasis-Ye chi_A constant (pp. 5-6, 8, 10, 22).
writing: Abstract states the trade-off plainly (as stable as Cholesky, nearly as efficient as SMW); counterexample in §2 before the method; theory followed by a computational-evidence subsection (§4.2); conclusion concedes speed (pp. 1, 5-6, 16, 34).
limits_future: Slightly slower than Schur complement, augmented system up to 3x faster with many dense columns, implementation differences between host codes; future: extend Theorem 4.4 to other D and general convex IPMs (done in S058) (pp. 29, 34).

method_links.note: keeps normal equations + sparse Cholesky and changes only dense-column handling, reusing classical rank-one updates (Bennett; Fletcher-Powell) and Wright's pivot skipping

title: Product-form Cholesky factorization in interior point methods for second-order cone programming
contribution: Extends product-form Cholesky factorization to SOCP normal equations (sparse plus low-rank with additions and subtractions), derives and costs five update variants, and proves Cholesky and product-form factors stay bounded as mu -> 0 for iterates near the central path, with a counterexample off it (pp. 1-3, 8, 14, 19-24).
problem_entry: Large cones make SOCP normal equations dense (sparse plus low rank); SMW is unstable on most SOCP problems even random nondegenerate ones; the LP analysis does not carry over directly (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Product-form LDL^T updates for V S V^T with indefinite diagonal S, based on 1960s-70s Bennett and Fletcher-Powell updates; rank-1 variants cheapest, rank-k Bennett for parallel machines (pp. 2, 8, 13-14).
assumptions: Iterates converge to a strictly complementary solution and stay in a central neighbourhood, x(mu) = x* + O(mu); purely primal case analysed for simplicity (pp. 15, 17, 19).
proof_devices: eigen-structure of the SOCP scaling matrix gives three eigenvalue rate classes (§4.1, Table 2, pp. 15-16)
smallest-bad-index contradiction reused from S050 (Theorem 1, pp. 19-20)
3x3 counterexample trajectory off the central path where L grows unboundedly, naming the failing lemma (§5, pp. 23-24)
experiments: SeDuMi 1.04 on 3 random and DIMACS SOCP problems: sizes of L entries (none above 10,000; filtinf1 with SDP the exception for >1,000) and times with/without PFCF; no SMW comparison since SeDuMi lacks it (pp. 24-26).
positioning: Sequel to S050 (ref [11]); SMW criticised as unstable (citing [2]); Sturm's SDP example cited as similar growth phenomenon (pp. 2, 24).
writing: Intro enumerates exactly why SOCP is harder than LP (subtractions, extra O(1) eigenvalues, bad scaling); work table for all variants; no conclusion section (pp. 2-3, 14, 26).
limits_future: Needs central neighbourhood (counterexample), SDP not covered without major revision, pivot skipping never needed; no future work stated (pp. 22-25).

method_links.note: old update formulas kept, only product form new; LP analysis carried over and changed where SOCP breaks it
sparse + low-rank normal-equation structure exploited, savings stated as a function of cone sizes

title: Detecting Generic Visual Eventswith Temporal Cues
contribution: Generic visual event detection in broadcast news via bag-of-frames shot representation compared by Earth Mover's Distance (an LP) and multi-cue fusion by multiple kernel learning solved as an SOCP (pp. 1-4).
problem_entry: Event detection in unconstrained video, where object-centred methods need strong scene assumptions and feature-driven ones use low-level features; extends the authors' HMM-based work (p. 1).
key_idea: EMD between frame clusters as a shot distance turned into an exponential kernel; MKL with shared support-vector weights and learned kernel weights (pp. 2-4).
assumptions: Shot-level binary labels; 33 concept-detector confidences per frame as descriptors (pp. 2, 4).
experiments: TRECVID-2005 dev set (~80 h, >69,000 shots, 1/3 held out), 13 LSCOM events, AP@1000; EMD more than doubles AP over static baseline, MKL +5% mean AP over early fusion but degrades some events (pp. 4-5).
positioning: Positions against object-centred and feature-driven event detection and early/late fusion; uses Bach-Lanckriet-Jordan MKL and Rubner et al. EMD (pp. 1, 3-4).
writing: Two-part contribution stated in the abstract and intro; results explained mechanistically (sparsity of the EMD flow; lost flexibility in MKL) (pp. 1, 4-5).
limits_future: O(n^2)/O(kn^2) kernel memory, MKL sometimes worse; future: predict which fusion suits which concept, joint program for kernel and SV weights (p. 5).

transferable: Report per-class gains and losses of a new fusion component and explain the loss mechanism (p. 5).

quotes.text: While MKL can increase average precision by 10 ∼ 200% for 8 out of the 13 target events, yet it sometimes degrades the performance compared to early- and late- fusion.

title: Rock Physics and Depositional History from Seismic Matching–A Model Study
contribution: A proof-of-concept study that fits basin-model (Basin2) and petrophysics parameters to synthetic seismic data by wrapping the forward chain in derivative-free and gradient-based optimizers, after replacing a multimodal least-squares misfit with a smoother functional (pp. 1-4).
problem_entry: Ill-posed, costly inverse problem of matching seismic phase and amplitude by adjusting sedimentary parameters; model study on a synthetic ground truth with 26 parameters (p. 1).
key_idea: Compare DFO, NEWUOA, ASA, IPOPT, CBB/CGCBB and LMDIF; diagnose spurious local minima of the least-squares misfit and switch to a two-stage split and a smooth envelope-of-envelope functional, adding 20 petrophysics unknowns (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: None formal; weighted sum-of-squares Basin2-loop functional (p. 3).
experiments: Basin2-loop convergence from several starting guesses (Fig. 5, not in text) and full-loop fits by ASA and NEWUOA needing well over a thousand iterations (pp. 3-4).
positioning: Extends Imhof-Sharma; cites differential semblance (Symes; Stolk-Symes) as the provably smooth functional they want to adopt (pp. 1, 3-4).
writing: Narrative engineering report with candid hedges ('perhaps unnecessarily', 'While not ideal') (p. 3).
limits_future: Next: differential-semblance functional, scaling and preconditioning, stochastic exploration of acceptable parameter sets, field data (p. 4).

title: Mathematical Programming in Machine Learning and Data Mining
contribution: BIRS workshop report (Banff, Jan 2007) that frames ML/DM problems as optimization, lists open problems by topic (kernels, structured prediction, SDP, clustering, complexity), collects talk abstracts and participant reports on follow-up work (pp. 1-10).
problem_entry: The MP and ML/DM communities are disjoint with no shared venues; the workshop aims to identify new problems and match them with solution approaches (p. 2).
key_idea: Report structure: overview, open problems, talk abstracts, participants' progress reports, outcome (pp. 1-10).
positioning: Places the workshop after 2005 workshops and a 2006 JMLR special topic on ML and large-scale optimization; cites Fine-Scheinberg 2001 and Scheinberg 2006 among MP-community SVM implementations (pp. 2, 11-12).
writing: Organizers' report; open problems stated per topic; Scheinberg's own signed section is short and concrete (visits, talks, ideas taken) (pp. 2-3, 9).
limits_future: Stated open problems: good kernels, l1 kernelization, SDP cost, relevance of worst-case accurate-solution complexity to generalization (pp. 2-3).
